subject_session: 8 sessions pooled; example figures use session 721123822
stated_limitation: Two results deserve qualification rather than being smoothed over. Visual thalamus is not at the null: 40 to 60 percent of LGd and LP units reach significance... Separately, 14 percent of hippocampal units reach significance, which is above the 5 percent expected by chance. The GLM suggests why: hippocampal firing is strongly modulated by running speed, and any residual coupling between behavioural state and the stimulus sequence produces weak apparent tuning.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000021 Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels is the canonical dataset for cortical orientation selectivity, with simultaneously recorded hippocampal units supplying a built-in negative control.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile with explicit Allen-default QC filtering, column-selective loading, and a guarded sort to keep per-unit metadata aligned with the TsGroup.
justification.analysis: Resultant-vector OSI/DSI with correct angle-doubling, a within-block shuffle null, split-half reliability, cross-stimulus replication, a running-speed GLM, and shuffle-controlled decoding together form an exemplary treatment.
justification.correctness: Every headline number reproduces exactly from the committed CSVs, is internally consistent with the figures, and rests on adequate samples and appropriate tests.
justification.figures: Figures show the bilobed orientation signature clearly with labeled units and sample sizes, and example cells are ranked by OSI (the effect itself) and honestly labeled as the most selective.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence and the write-up names its specific weaknesses (thalamic tuning, the above-chance hippocampal fraction and its GLM-based explanation) rather than smoothing them over.
justification.verdict: Rigorous, reproducible, well-controlled, and honestly reported; I would take this result and move on.
